t: A gum stick sized Linux computer with Wi-Fi 6 and a camera port.
steps: Buy the board from Arace, the Radxa partner store, or a reseller such as AmeriDroid. Pick a version with the header soldered on for pin projects.
Get a 5 volt 2 amp USB-C power supply, a microSD card, a micro HDMI cable, and a USB-C adapter.
Download a Debian or Ubuntu image for the ZERO 3W from the Radxa docs site.
Write the image to the microSD card with an image writing app.
Plug power into the USB-C OTG port and connect a screen and keyboard.
Follow the Radxa ZERO 3 getting started guide to join Wi-Fi.
Try a short Python script to take a photo with a Pi camera module.
meta: Open Board. From $20. A few stores.
